title: FlytWERX ACS Maneuver Standards Checker Data

acs.documentTitle: Private Pilot for Airplane Category Airman Certification Standards

page.disclaimer: This checker summarizes selected FAA ACS performance standards for training and debrief use. Always use the current official FAA ACS and the applicable POH/AFM. FlytWERX data supports review and does not replace evaluator judgment or approved aircraft indications.

normal-takeoff.name: Normal Takeoff
normal-takeoff.objective: Normal takeoff, climb operations, and rejected takeoff procedures.

metrics.label: Climb Airspeed
metrics.description: Maintain the manufacturer's recommended climb speed or VY.

metrics.label: Lift-Off
metrics.description: Rotate and lift off at the manufacturer's recommended airspeed.

metrics.label: Wind Correction
metrics.description: Maintain directional control and proper wind-drift correction throughout takeoff and climb.
metrics.note: Crosswind control is part of the normal takeoff task.

metrics.label: Configuration
metrics.description: Configure the airplane in accordance with manufacturer guidance.

criteria: Complete the appropriate checklist and radio calls.
Verify the correct runway and determine wind direction.
Position the flight controls for the existing wind.
Align with the runway centerline, apply takeoff power smoothly, and verify proper indications.
Rotate at the recommended airspeed and establish the recommended climb speed or VY within +10/-5 knots.
Maintain directional control, wind-drift correction, and the appropriate climb configuration.

reviewVariables.label: CENTERLINE
reviewVariables.text: Review directional-control trend from takeoff roll through initial climb.

reviewVariables.label: AIRSPEED
reviewVariables.text: Review how quickly the airplane captured and stabilized near the recommended climb speed.

reviewVariables.label: WIND
reviewVariables.text: Compare control and ground-track changes with the reported crosswind.

reviewVariables.label: ROTATION
reviewVariables.text: Review the transition from ground roll to liftoff for abrupt or delayed pitch change.

reviewVariables.label: CLIMB
reviewVariables.text: Look for airspeed or vertical-path instability after liftoff.

reviewVariables.label: CONFIGURATION
reviewVariables.text: Confirm configuration changes were consistent with the aircraft procedure and lesson notes.

source.documentTitle: Private Pilot for Airplane Category Airman Certification Standards

crosswind-takeoff.name: Crosswind Takeoff
crosswind-takeoff.displayNote: The Private Pilot ACS does not create a separate crosswind-takeoff task. Crosswind knowledge and control are evaluated within Normal Takeoff and Climb.

source.documentTitle: Private Pilot for Airplane Category Airman Certification Standards

soft-field-takeoff.name: Soft-Field Takeoff
soft-field-takeoff.objective: Soft-field takeoff, climb operations, and rejected takeoff procedures.

metrics.label: Climb Airspeed
metrics.description: Maintain VX or VY, as appropriate.

metrics.label: Lift-Off
metrics.description: Lift off at the lowest possible airspeed and remain in ground effect while accelerating.

metrics.label: Ground Effect
metrics.description: Remain in ground effect while accelerating to VX or VY, as appropriate.

metrics.label: Wind Correction
metrics.description: Maintain directional control and proper wind-drift correction throughout takeoff and climb.

criteria: Complete the appropriate checklist, radio calls, runway verification, and wind assessment.
Position the controls for wind and taxi into takeoff position without stopping while applying power smoothly.
Transfer weight from the wheels to the wings as rapidly as practical.
Lift off at the lowest possible airspeed and remain in ground effect while accelerating.
Establish VX or VY as appropriate and maintain the selected airspeed within +10/-5 knots.
Configure after a positive rate of climb or as directed by the manufacturer, while maintaining directional control.

reviewVariables.label: GROUND ROLL
reviewVariables.text: Review whether the airplane remained moving and whether control inputs reduced wheel loading.

reviewVariables.label: LIFT-OFF
reviewVariables.text: Review the pitch transition and the point where the airplane became airborne.

reviewVariables.label: GROUND EFFECT
reviewVariables.text: Look for premature climb or excess acceleration while remaining close to the surface.

reviewVariables.label: AIRSPEED
reviewVariables.text: Review capture and stability of VX or VY after leaving ground effect.

reviewVariables.label: WIND
reviewVariables.text: Review directional-control and drift correction through the takeoff and climb.

reviewVariables.label: CONFIGURATION
reviewVariables.text: Compare configuration timing with the POH/AFM and instructor notes.

source.documentTitle: Private Pilot for Airplane Category Airman Certification Standards

short-field-takeoff.name: Short-Field Takeoff

metrics.label: Obstacle / VX
metrics.description: Maintain the recommended obstacle-clearance airspeed or VX until obstacle clearance or 50 feet AGL when simulated.

metrics.label: VY
metrics.description: After obstacle clearance, accelerate to and maintain VY.

metrics.label: Takeoff Area
metrics.description: Use the maximum available takeoff area.

metrics.label: Simulated Obstacle
metrics.description: Transition after the obstacle is cleared or at 50 feet AGL when an obstacle is simulated.

criteria: Complete the appropriate checklist, radio calls, runway verification, wind assessment, and control positioning.
Use the maximum available takeoff area and set maximum-performance power before brake release.
Confirm takeoff power and proper indications before rotation.
Rotate at the recommended airspeed and accelerate to the recommended obstacle-clearance speed or VX within +10/-5 knots.
Maintain the obstacle-clearance speed or VX within +10/-5 knots until clear, then accelerate to VY within +10/-5 knots.
Configure per manufacturer guidance and maintain directional control and wind-drift correction.

reviewVariables.label: RUNWAY USE
reviewVariables.text: Review whether the maximum available takeoff area was used.

reviewVariables.label: POWER
reviewVariables.text: Review the timing between brake release, power stabilization, and rotation.

reviewVariables.label: VX / OBSTACLE
reviewVariables.text: Review airspeed stability during the obstacle-clearance segment.

reviewVariables.label: TRANSITION
reviewVariables.text: Review the transition from obstacle-clearance speed to VY.

reviewVariables.label: DIRECTION
reviewVariables.text: Review centerline and wind-drift control during the takeoff and climb.

reviewVariables.label: CONFIGURATION
reviewVariables.text: Review when configuration changed relative to positive rate and obstacle clearance.

source.documentTitle: Private Pilot for Airplane Category Airman Certification Standards
source.taskName: Short-Field Takeoff and Maximum Performance Climb

normal-landing.name: Normal Landing
normal-landing.objective: Normal approach and landing with proper use and coordination of flight controls.

metrics.label: Approach Airspeed
metrics.description: Maintain the manufacturer's published approach airspeed, or the ACS fallback if none is published.
metrics.note: ACS tolerance: +10 / -5 KTS with gust factor applied.

metrics.label: Touchdown
metrics.description: Touch down on or within 400 feet beyond the specified point.

metrics.label: Side Drift
metrics.description: Touch down with no side drift.

metrics.label: Alignment
metrics.description: Longitudinal axis aligned with and over the runway centerline or landing path.

criteria: Complete the appropriate checklist and radio calls, verify the runway, and scan for traffic and obstructions.
Select and aim for a suitable touchdown point considering wind, surface, and obstructions.
Establish the recommended configuration, airspeed, trim, and a stabilized approach.
Maintain the published approach airspeed within +10/-5 knots with gust factor applied.
Maintain directional control and crosswind correction, then make smooth and timely roundout and touchdown inputs.
Touch down on or within 400 feet beyond the specified point with no side drift and proper centerline alignment; go around if the approach becomes unsafe or outside tolerance.

reviewVariables.label: AIRSPEED
reviewVariables.text: Review the final-approach speed trend and how quickly deviations were corrected.

reviewVariables.label: PATH
reviewVariables.text: Review whether the approach remained stabilized toward the selected touchdown point.

reviewVariables.label: CENTERLINE
reviewVariables.text: Look for lateral drift or alignment changes on final and during touchdown.

reviewVariables.label: TOUCHDOWN
reviewVariables.text: Compare touchdown location with the selected point and the 400-foot ACS window.

reviewVariables.label: CROSSWIND
reviewVariables.text: Review bank, heading, and ground track for evidence of effective wind correction.

reviewVariables.label: GO-AROUND
reviewVariables.text: Review whether an unstable or unsafe trend should have triggered a go-around.

source.documentTitle: Private Pilot for Airplane Category Airman Certification Standards

crosswind-landing.name: Crosswind Landing
crosswind-landing.displayNote: The Private Pilot ACS does not create a separate crosswind-landing task. Crosswind correction is evaluated within the applicable landing task.

source.documentTitle: Private Pilot for Airplane Category Airman Certification Standards

soft-field-landing.name: Soft-Field Landing

metrics.label: Approach Airspeed
metrics.description: Maintain the published approach airspeed or ACS fallback.
metrics.note: ACS tolerance: +10 / -5 KTS with gust factor applied.

metrics.label: Sink Rate
metrics.description: Touch down with minimum sink rate.

metrics.label: Side Drift
metrics.description: Touch down with no side drift.

metrics.label: Alignment
metrics.description: Longitudinal axis aligned with the center of the runway.

criteria: Complete the appropriate checklist and radio calls, verify the runway, and scan for traffic and obstructions.
Select and aim for a suitable touchdown point and establish a stabilized approach.
Maintain the published approach airspeed within +10/-5 knots with gust factor applied.
Maintain directional control and crosswind correction throughout the approach and landing.
Touch down at a proper pitch attitude with minimum sink rate, no side drift, and runway-centerline alignment.
Maintain the manufacturer-recommended elevator position during rollout and sufficient speed to avoid sinking into the soft surface.

reviewVariables.label: AIRSPEED
reviewVariables.text: Review the approach-speed trend through touchdown.

reviewVariables.label: SINK RATE
reviewVariables.text: Review the vertical-speed trend immediately before touchdown.

reviewVariables.label: PITCH
reviewVariables.text: Review pitch change during roundout and touchdown.

reviewVariables.label: CENTERLINE
reviewVariables.text: Review lateral drift and alignment during touchdown.

reviewVariables.label: ROLLOUT
reviewVariables.text: Review speed decay and directional control after touchdown.

reviewVariables.label: GO-AROUND
reviewVariables.text: Look for unstable trends that should have led to a timely go-around.

source.documentTitle: Private Pilot for Airplane Category Airman Certification Standards

short-field-landing.name: Short-Field Landing

metrics.label: Approach Airspeed
metrics.description: Maintain the published approach airspeed or ACS fallback.
metrics.note: ACS tolerance: +10 / -5 KTS with gust factor applied.

metrics.label: Touchdown
metrics.description: Touch down on or within 200 feet beyond the specified point, threshold markings, or runway numbers.

metrics.label: Float
metrics.description: Touch down with minimum float.

metrics.label: Side Drift
metrics.description: Touch down with no side drift and proper centerline alignment.

criteria: Complete the appropriate checklist and radio calls, verify the runway, and scan for traffic and obstructions.
Select and aim for a suitable touchdown point and establish a stabilized approach.
Maintain the published approach airspeed within +10/-5 knots with gust factor applied.
Maintain directional control and crosswind correction throughout the approach and landing.
Touch down on or within 200 feet beyond the specified point with minimum float, no side drift, and centerline alignment.
Use manufacturer-recommended configuration and braking procedures and execute a timely go-around if needed.

reviewVariables.label: AIRSPEED
reviewVariables.text: Review whether final-approach speed stayed inside the tolerance band.

reviewVariables.label: TOUCHDOWN
reviewVariables.text: Compare touchdown location with the specified point and 200-foot ACS window.

reviewVariables.label: FLOAT
reviewVariables.text: Review whether excess energy produced unnecessary float.

reviewVariables.label: CENTERLINE
reviewVariables.text: Review alignment and lateral drift through touchdown.

reviewVariables.label: BRAKING
reviewVariables.text: Document braking and configuration context when available; do not infer unrecorded inputs.

reviewVariables.label: GO-AROUND
reviewVariables.text: Review whether the approach remained safe and within tolerance.

source.documentTitle: Private Pilot for Airplane Category Airman Certification Standards

forward-slip-to-landing.name: Forward Slip to a Landing

metrics.label: Touchdown
metrics.description: Touch down on or within 400 feet beyond the specified point.

metrics.label: Side Drift
metrics.description: Touch down with no side drift.

metrics.label: Alignment
metrics.description: Longitudinal axis aligned with and over the runway centerline or landing path.

metrics.label: Ground Track
metrics.description: Maintain a ground track aligned with the runway centerline or landing path.

criteria: Complete the appropriate checklist and radio calls and plan a suitable flightpath and touchdown point.
Position the airplane appropriately and configure it correctly.
Use a forward slip as necessary while considering wind and airplane limitations.
Correlate crosswind with slip direction and transition to a sideslip before touchdown when necessary.
Touch down on or within 400 feet beyond the specified point with no side drift and proper longitudinal alignment.
Maintain a ground track aligned with the runway centerline or landing path.

reviewVariables.label: ENERGY
reviewVariables.text: Review how the slip changed descent path without creating an excessive airspeed trend.

reviewVariables.label: SLIP
reviewVariables.text: Review bank, heading, and ground track during the forward slip.

reviewVariables.label: TRANSITION
reviewVariables.text: Review the transition from forward slip to touchdown alignment.

reviewVariables.label: TOUCHDOWN
reviewVariables.text: Compare touchdown location with the selected point and 400-foot window.

reviewVariables.label: CENTERLINE
reviewVariables.text: Review ground track and longitudinal alignment.

reviewVariables.label: WIND
reviewVariables.text: Compare the slip direction and final alignment with the reported wind.

source.documentTitle: Private Pilot for Airplane Category Airman Certification Standards

go-around.name: Go-Around / Rejected Landing

metrics.label: Climb Airspeed
metrics.description: Transition to VX or VY as appropriate and maintain VY to a safe maneuvering altitude.

metrics.label: Decision
metrics.description: Make a timely decision to discontinue the approach.

metrics.label: Configuration
metrics.description: Configure after positive rate or in accordance with manufacturer instructions.

metrics.label: Wind Correction
metrics.description: Maintain directional control and wind-drift correction throughout the climb.

criteria: Complete the appropriate checklist and radio calls.
Make a timely decision to discontinue the approach.
Apply takeoff power immediately and transition to VX or VY as appropriate within +10/-5 knots.
Configure after a positive rate of climb or as directed by the manufacturer.
Maneuver as necessary to avoid conflicting traffic.
Maintain VY within +10/-5 knots to a safe maneuvering altitude with directional control and wind correction.

reviewVariables.label: DECISION
reviewVariables.text: Review when the go-around decision was made relative to the developing approach.

reviewVariables.label: POWER
reviewVariables.text: Review the transition from approach power to climb.

reviewVariables.label: AIRSPEED
reviewVariables.text: Review capture of VX or VY and whether speed stabilized within tolerance.

reviewVariables.label: CONFIGURATION
reviewVariables.text: Review timing of configuration changes relative to positive rate.

reviewVariables.label: DIRECTION
reviewVariables.text: Review centerline, drift, and traffic-avoidance maneuvering.

reviewVariables.label: CLIMB
reviewVariables.text: Review the vertical path and speed trend through the safe maneuvering altitude.

source.documentTitle: Private Pilot for Airplane Category Airman Certification Standards

steep-turns.name: Steep Turns

metrics.label: Altitude
metrics.description: Maintain entry altitude.

metrics.label: Airspeed
metrics.description: Maintain entry airspeed.

metrics.label: Bank
metrics.description: Maintain approximately 45° of bank.
metrics.note: ACS allowable deviation from established bank: ±5°

metrics.label: Rollout Heading
metrics.description: Roll out on the entry heading.

criteria: Clear the area.
Establish the manufacturer's recommended airspeed or, if none is available, an airspeed not exceeding VA.
Roll into a coordinated 360-degree steep turn using approximately 45 degrees of bank.
Perform the task in the opposite direction as specified by the evaluator.
Maintain entry altitude within ±100 feet, airspeed within ±10 knots, and bank within ±5 degrees.
Roll out on the entry heading within ±10 degrees.

reviewVariables.label: ALTITUDE
reviewVariables.text: Review where altitude drift began and whether it was associated with bank or pitch changes.

reviewVariables.label: AIRSPEED
reviewVariables.text: Review speed stability through entry, the turn, and rollout.

reviewVariables.label: BANK
reviewVariables.text: Review how quickly and smoothly approximately 45 degrees of bank was established and maintained.

reviewVariables.label: COORDINATION
reviewVariables.text: Use available data and instructor observation to assess slip/skid tendencies.

reviewVariables.label: ROLLOUT
reviewVariables.text: Review rollout timing and heading accuracy.

reviewVariables.label: CONTROL INPUTS
reviewVariables.text: Look for abrupt corrections or oscillations across bank, pitch, and heading.

source.documentTitle: Private Pilot for Airplane Category Airman Certification Standards

rectangular-course.name: Rectangular Course

metrics.label: Altitude
metrics.description: Maintain maneuver altitude.

metrics.label: Airspeed
metrics.description: Maintain maneuver airspeed.

metrics.label: Entry Altitude
metrics.description: Enter the rectangular course at the ACS-specified altitude band.

metrics.label: Ground Track
metrics.description: Apply adequate wind-drift correction to maintain the rectangular ground track.

criteria: Clear the area and select a suitable reference area.
Enter a left or right rectangular pattern 600 to 1,000 feet AGL at an appropriate distance, 45 degrees to the downwind leg.
Apply wind-drift correction during straight and turning flight.
Maintain the intended rectangular ground track.
Divide attention between airplane control, traffic avoidance, and ground track while maintaining coordinated flight.
Maintain altitude within ±100 feet and airspeed within ±10 knots.

reviewVariables.label: GROUND TRACK
reviewVariables.text: Review spacing from each side of the rectangular reference area.

reviewVariables.label: WIND
reviewVariables.text: Review whether wind correction changed appropriately on each leg.

reviewVariables.label: BANK
reviewVariables.text: Review turn rate and bank changes as groundspeed changed.

reviewVariables.label: ALTITUDE
reviewVariables.text: Review altitude stability while attention was primarily outside.

reviewVariables.label: AIRSPEED
reviewVariables.text: Review airspeed stability through turns and straight segments.

reviewVariables.label: COORDINATION
reviewVariables.text: Combine recorded trends with instructor observation for coordinated-flight assessment.

source.documentTitle: Private Pilot for Airplane Category Airman Certification Standards

s-turns.name: S-Turns

metrics.label: Altitude
metrics.description: Maintain maneuver altitude.

metrics.label: Airspeed
metrics.description: Maintain maneuver airspeed.

metrics.label: Entry Altitude
metrics.description: Enter perpendicular to the selected reference line.

metrics.label: Turn Reversal
metrics.description: Reverse the turn directly over the selected reference line.

criteria: Clear the area and select a suitable reference line.
Enter perpendicular to the reference line 600 to 1,000 feet AGL at an appropriate distance.
Apply adequate wind-drift correction to maintain a constant-radius turn on each side of the line.
Reverse the turn directly over the selected reference line.
Divide attention between airplane control, traffic avoidance, and ground track while maintaining coordinated flight.
Maintain altitude within ±100 feet and airspeed within ±10 knots.

reviewVariables.label: GROUND TRACK
reviewVariables.text: Compare the radius and symmetry of the two semicircles.

reviewVariables.label: CROSSING
reviewVariables.text: Review whether turn reversals occurred directly over the reference line.

reviewVariables.label: WIND
reviewVariables.text: Review whether bank and turn rate changed appropriately with groundspeed.

reviewVariables.label: ALTITUDE
reviewVariables.text: Review altitude stability while attention was divided outside.

reviewVariables.label: AIRSPEED
reviewVariables.text: Review airspeed through each turn and reversal.

reviewVariables.label: COORDINATION
reviewVariables.text: Combine recorded trends with instructor observation for coordinated-flight assessment.

source.documentTitle: Private Pilot for Airplane Category Airman Certification Standards

turns-around-a-point.name: Turns Around a Point

metrics.label: Altitude
metrics.description: Maintain maneuver altitude.

metrics.label: Airspeed
metrics.description: Maintain maneuver airspeed.

metrics.label: Entry Altitude
metrics.description: Enter at an appropriate distance from the selected point.

metrics.label: Radius
metrics.description: Apply wind-drift correction to maintain a constant-radius turn.

criteria: Clear the area and select a suitable reference point.
Enter at an appropriate distance from the reference point 600 to 1,000 feet AGL.
Apply adequate wind-drift correction to maintain a constant-radius turn around the point.
Complete turns in the direction specified by the evaluator.
Divide attention between airplane control, traffic avoidance, and ground track while maintaining coordinated flight.
Maintain altitude within ±100 feet and airspeed within ±10 knots.

reviewVariables.label: RADIUS
reviewVariables.text: Review how consistently the ground-track radius was maintained.

reviewVariables.label: WIND
reviewVariables.text: Review bank and turn-rate changes as groundspeed changed around the point.

reviewVariables.label: ALTITUDE
reviewVariables.text: Review altitude stability while attention was divided outside.

reviewVariables.label: AIRSPEED
reviewVariables.text: Review speed stability through the full turn.

reviewVariables.label: BANK
reviewVariables.text: Review whether bank changes were smooth and appropriate to wind correction.

reviewVariables.label: COORDINATION
reviewVariables.text: Combine recorded trends with instructor observation for coordinated-flight assessment.

source.documentTitle: Private Pilot for Airplane Category Airman Certification Standards

slow-flight.name: Slow Flight
slow-flight.objective: Maneuvering during slow flight in cruise configuration.

metrics.label: Altitude
metrics.description: Maintain the specified altitude.

metrics.label: Airspeed
metrics.description: Maintain the specified slow-flight airspeed.

metrics.label: Heading
metrics.description: Maintain the specified heading.

metrics.label: Bank
metrics.description: Maintain the specified angle of bank.

criteria: Clear the area.
Select an entry altitude that permits completion no lower than 1,500 feet AGL for ASEL.
Establish and maintain an airspeed where further increase in angle of attack, load factor, or reduction in power would produce a stall warning.
Perform coordinated straight-and-level flight, turns, climbs, and descents in the configuration specified by the evaluator without a stall warning.
Maintain altitude within ±100 feet, heading within ±10 degrees, airspeed +10/-0 knots, and bank within ±10 degrees.
Recognize and correct any momentary stall warning appropriately.

reviewVariables.label: ALTITUDE
reviewVariables.text: Review where altitude drift began and whether the correction stabilized the trend.

reviewVariables.label: AIRSPEED
reviewVariables.text: Review how consistently the selected slow-flight airspeed was maintained above the stall-warning condition.

reviewVariables.label: HEADING
reviewVariables.text: Review directional drift during straight flight and maneuver changes.

reviewVariables.label: BANK
reviewVariables.text: Review bank stability during turns and transitions.

reviewVariables.label: COORDINATION
reviewVariables.text: Use instructor observation and available data to assess coordination.

reviewVariables.label: STALL MARGIN
reviewVariables.text: Review any recorded or observed stall-warning event and the promptness of correction.

source.documentTitle: Private Pilot for Airplane Category Airman Certification Standards

power-off-stall.name: Power-Off Stall

metrics.label: Heading
metrics.description: If inducing the stall in straight flight, maintain the specified heading.

metrics.label: Bank
metrics.description: If inducing the stall in turning flight, use no more than 20° bank and maintain the specified bank within ±10°.

metrics.label: Minimum Completion Altitude
metrics.description: Select an entry altitude that allows completion no lower than 1,500 feet AGL for ASEL.

metrics.label: Recovery
metrics.description: Acknowledge impending-stall cues, allow a full stall, then recover promptly using POH/AFM procedures.
metrics.note: No universal altitude-loss tolerance is published.

criteria: Clear the area and select an entry altitude that permits completion no lower than 1,500 feet AGL for ASEL.
Configure in the approach or landing configuration specified by the evaluator and maintain coordinated flight.
Establish a stabilized descent and smoothly increase pitch to induce the stall.
Maintain heading within ±10 degrees in straight flight, or bank not exceeding 20 degrees and within ±10 degrees of the specified bank in turning flight.
Acknowledge impending-stall cues, recover promptly after a full stall, and use the POH/AFM recovery procedure.
Reconfigure as recommended, accelerate to VX or VY, and return to the evaluator-specified altitude, heading, and airspeed.

reviewVariables.label: ENTRY
reviewVariables.text: Review configuration, descent stability, and coordination before stall induction.

reviewVariables.label: HEADING / BANK
reviewVariables.text: Review directional and bank control while inducing the stall.

reviewVariables.label: STALL CUES
reviewVariables.text: Document observed stall-warning cues; telemetry alone may not capture them.

reviewVariables.label: RECOVERY
reviewVariables.text: Review timing and smoothness of the recovery sequence.

reviewVariables.label: AIRSPEED
reviewVariables.text: Review acceleration toward VX or VY after recovery.

reviewVariables.label: ALTITUDE
reviewVariables.text: Review altitude loss as debrief context; the ACS does not set one universal recovery-loss tolerance for this task.

source.documentTitle: Private Pilot for Airplane Category Airman Certification Standards

power-on-stall.name: Power-On Stall

metrics.label: Heading
metrics.description: If inducing the stall in straight flight, maintain the specified heading.

metrics.label: Bank
metrics.description: If inducing the stall in turning flight, use no more than 20° bank and maintain the specified bank within ±10°.

metrics.label: Power
metrics.description: Set power assigned by the evaluator to no less than 65 percent.

metrics.label: Minimum Completion Altitude
metrics.description: Select an entry altitude that allows completion no lower than 1,500 feet AGL for ASEL.

criteria: Clear the area and select an entry altitude that permits completion no lower than 1,500 feet AGL for ASEL.
Establish the takeoff, departure, or cruise configuration specified by the evaluator and maintain coordinated flight.
Set assigned power to no less than 65 percent and smoothly transition to the pitch attitude that induces a stall.
Maintain heading within ±10 degrees in straight flight, or bank not exceeding 20 degrees and within ±10 degrees of the specified bank in turning flight.
Acknowledge impending-stall cues, recover promptly after a full stall, and use the POH/AFM recovery procedure.
Reconfigure as recommended, accelerate to VX or VY, and return to the evaluator-specified altitude, heading, and airspeed.

reviewVariables.label: ENTRY
reviewVariables.text: Review configuration, power application, and coordination before stall induction.

reviewVariables.label: HEADING / BANK
reviewVariables.text: Review directional and bank control while inducing the stall.

reviewVariables.label: POWER
reviewVariables.text: Document the assigned power context; portable telemetry may not record engine power directly.

reviewVariables.label: STALL CUES
reviewVariables.text: Document observed stall-warning cues; telemetry alone may not capture them.

reviewVariables.label: RECOVERY
reviewVariables.text: Review timing and smoothness of the recovery sequence.

reviewVariables.label: AIRSPEED
reviewVariables.text: Review acceleration toward VX or VY after recovery.

source.documentTitle: Private Pilot for Airplane Category Airman Certification Standards

emergency-descent.name: Emergency Descent

metrics.label: Airspeed
metrics.description: Maintain the appropriate scenario/POH airspeed.

metrics.label: Level-Off Altitude
metrics.description: Level off at the altitude specified by the evaluator.

metrics.label: Bank
metrics.description: Use 30° to 45° of bank to maintain positive load factors during the descent.

metrics.label: Configuration
metrics.description: Use the appropriate configuration for the scenario.

criteria: Clear the area.
Establish the appropriate airspeed and configuration for the scenario and POH/AFM.
Maintain orientation, divide attention appropriately, and plan a smooth recovery.
Use 30 to 45 degrees of bank to maintain positive load factors during the descent.
Maintain the appropriate airspeed within +0/-10 knots and level off within ±100 feet of the specified altitude.
Complete appropriate checklists, radio calls, and resource-management actions.

reviewVariables.label: AIRSPEED
reviewVariables.text: Review capture and stability of the scenario-appropriate emergency-descent airspeed.

reviewVariables.label: BANK
reviewVariables.text: Review whether bank stayed within the 30–45 degree ACS range.

reviewVariables.label: VERTICAL PATH
reviewVariables.text: Review descent-rate trend and whether the recovery was smooth.

reviewVariables.label: LEVEL-OFF
reviewVariables.text: Review altitude capture against the ±100-foot standard.

reviewVariables.label: ORIENTATION
reviewVariables.text: Review heading/ground track to support discussion of orientation and traffic avoidance.

reviewVariables.label: CONFIGURATION
reviewVariables.text: Document the POH/AFM configuration and checklist context used during the scenario.

source.documentTitle: Private Pilot for Airplane Category Airman Certification Standards

emergency-approach-and-landing.name: Emergency Approach and Landing

metrics.label: Best Glide
metrics.description: Maintain the recommended best-glide airspeed.

metrics.label: Landing Area
metrics.description: Select a suitable landing area considering altitude, wind, terrain, obstructions, and glide distance.

metrics.label: Flightpath
metrics.description: Plan and follow a flightpath to the selected landing area.

metrics.label: Checklist
metrics.description: Complete the appropriate emergency checklist.

criteria: Establish and maintain the recommended best-glide airspeed within ±10 knots.
Configure the airplane in accordance with the POH/AFM and existing conditions.
Select a suitable landing area considering altitude, wind, terrain, obstructions, and available glide distance.
Plan and follow a flightpath to the selected landing area.
Prepare for landing as specified by the evaluator.
Complete the appropriate checklist.

reviewVariables.label: BEST GLIDE
reviewVariables.text: Review how quickly best-glide speed was established and how steadily it was maintained.

reviewVariables.label: FIELD SELECTION
reviewVariables.text: Use instructor observation and recorded position to discuss the selected landing area and alternatives.

reviewVariables.label: FLIGHTPATH
reviewVariables.text: Review whether the path preserved reachability to the selected area.

reviewVariables.label: WIND
reviewVariables.text: Compare glide path and groundspeed with the wind used during the exercise.

reviewVariables.label: MANEUVERING
reviewVariables.text: Review bank and airspeed changes during the simulated emergency pattern.

reviewVariables.label: CHECKLIST
reviewVariables.text: Document checklist timing and division of attention; telemetry alone cannot prove checklist completion.

source.documentTitle: Private Pilot for Airplane Category Airman Certification Standards
